![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203245/assets/804c19a20b6f47707a07c7bdcee3cbd727eec2c270109e30eb55d949ace8edf0.png)

Calculate the value of $BC$ to the nearest integer.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

Notice that we are given the length of the leg $\overset{―}{AC}$ opposite to the given angle $∠B$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{BC}$ adjacent $∠B.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the adjacent leg is *tangent*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({20}^{∘}) & =\frac{2.91}{BC} \\ BC\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({20}^{∘}) & =2.91 \\ BC & =\frac{2.91}{\operatorname{tan}⁡({20}^{∘})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =\frac{2.91}{\operatorname{tan}⁡({20}^{∘})} \\  & =\frac{2.91}{(0.363\,97…)} \\  & =7.995\,15… \\  & ≈8,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.
